newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down but shake off Wall Street drop.
newsitem.headline: German shares down but shake off Wall Street drop.

text.p: German shares were modestly lower in early bourse dealings on Tuesday after shaking off the pressure of one of the worst one-day declines on Wall Street.
The 30-share DAX index was down 12.74 points at 3,741.98 points, which was well above the session low of 3,709.58 points reached at the outset of pre-bourse IBIS computer dealings.
"The market has come back very well and it shows we are in a relatively healthy position," said one Frankfurt trader.
"We are still likely to finish the day with losses but it will not be as bad as what happened in New York," he said.
Wall Street stocks ended down 2.50 percent after Japan's Prime Minister Ryuto Hashimoto commented on the potential sale by Japan of U.S. government securities.
The bout of profit-taking was the second largest single-day point drop in the history of the Dow Jones index.
German traders said the DAX index should find strong support at 3,700 points and few saw a chance of that level being broken in the near-term.
Instead, the DAX will likely stabilise between 3,725 and 3,750 points as traders square up books ahead of the end of the second quarter and for trading volumes to remain thin.

"International investors do not appear to be interested in the German market right now," said one Frankfurt trader. "The action after the early selling pressure appears to be mainly from domestic investors looking for bargains."
One share attracting buying attention was electronics group Siemens AG, which rose 2.05 marks to 105.25 marks and was outperforming the broader 30-share DAX.
"Siemens is withstanding the pressure very well and should keep outperforming the market," said one trader. "
But traders said chemical and banking sector shares were generally lower on a lack of enthusiasm for the sectors.
Germany's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank AG, was down 23 pfennigs at 97.45 marks, while chemical group Bayer AG was down 63 pfennigs at 67.82 marks.

German airline Lufthansa AG was down 90 pfennigs at 34.50 marks ahead of its annual general meeting on Thursday. A Lufthansa official said on Monday in Hong Kong that the airline was talking with major airlines to build a cargo alliance.
